analyst_view.overall: Early view: Villa have conceded seven goals in their last two games, losing 3-0 at Barcelona in the Champions League and then throwing away a 4-2 lead in stoppage time in a 4-4 draw at Old Trafford. Sunderland come in after a 1-0 win over Chelsea, but Granit Xhaka limped off early in that game with a suspected calf problem and his fitness is the main team news.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.8 goals. I lean slightly higher: Villa's defence has leaked seven in two games, while their attack is scoring, with Jackson, McGinn and Goretzka all on target at Old Trafford. Sunderland scored only from a penalty against Chelsea, but Villa are giving chances away to everyone right now.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.4 corners. I lean a little higher: Villa should have long spells of pressure at Villa Park against a Sunderland side that beat Chelsea by defending a first-half lead, and without Xhaka on the ball Sunderland may spend even more time in their own half.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.7 cards, 3.1 of them Sunderland's. I lean higher: Sunderland had six names in the book against Chelsea, including manager Regis Le Bris, and Jules Ahoka, who replaced Xhaka, was booked within 20 minutes. A stretched midfield away from home tends to bring more fouls.

shots.text: The numbers say 28.1 shots, 16.7 of them Villa's. That looks fair: Villa will dominate the ball at home, but Sunderland just held Chelsea scoreless, which pulls the other way. I keep the site's figure until the team news is clear.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.5 shots on target. I lean slightly higher: Villa's forwards are finding the target, with four goals at Old Trafford, and Sunderland's back line is missing Dan Ballard with a hamstring injury.
